panels.description: Application payload throughput per operation, summed across bench l2 initiators on mmgi0/mmgi1 and across warmup+measured -- unlike LMCache aggregate goodput below, which is measured-only. Warmup is real O_DIRECT I/O against the same devices and fabric NVMe RD/RDMA WR account for, so leaving it out understated this panel by up to ~3.5x during a multi-initiator sweep where hosts run warmup/measured out of phase with each other. Expect this to track NVMe RD/RDMA WR closely at all times, not just during a measured window. A rate() window straddling a warmup->measured transition still dips briefly, since each phase is its own counter starting from zero. Read and write goodput are deliberately not added together. For the clean steady-state number, use LMCache aggregate goodput below or the end-of-run JSON.
panels.title: LMCache

panels.description: Aggregate kernel read throughput off the eight md0 members, in bits/s. Shares a hue with RDMA WR: the two ends of the read path. Tracks LMCache to within 0.1% during a retrieve run. The storage stack section shows the same figure in bytes/s.
panels.title: NVMe RD

panels.description: Falcon acc_tele_field bytes_from_ulp_rc, summed across IPUs on MMG Target: payload the target pushes out to the fabric, which is what an initiator read turns into. Same bytes as the Falcon panel's WR series and as NVMe RD, one hop earlier. A direction counter, not a count of RDMA WRITE opcodes. The underlying counter latches every 30s - 34 of 40 consecutive 5s buckets were empty and the other 6 carried ~356 Gb/s each - so rate() beats against the latch period and sawtooths at any window width. This uses deriv() over 5m, a least-squares fit across every sample in the window, which reads as smooth as the payload itself (CV 1.7% against 1.9%) and within ~1% of goodput. clamp_min guards against the counter resetting, which deriv() would otherwise render as a negative spike.
panels.title: RDMA WR

panels.description: Aggregate kernel write throughput off the eight md0 members, in bits/s. Shares a hue with RDMA RD: the two ends of the write path. Reads 0 throughout a Load-only (retrieve) window, which is the expected result and not a dead query - check the operation names on LMCache to tell the two cases apart.
panels.title: NVMe WR

panels.description: Falcon acc_tele_field bytes_to_ulp, summed across IPUs on MMG Target: payload arriving from the fabric, which is what an initiator write turns into. Same bytes as the Falcon panel's RD series and as NVMe WR. Sits near zero throughout a Load-only window by construction. The underlying counter latches every 30s - 34 of 40 consecutive 5s buckets were empty and the other 6 carried ~356 Gb/s each - so rate() beats against the latch period and sawtooths at any window width. This uses deriv() over 5m, a least-squares fit across every sample in the window, which reads as smooth as the payload itself (CV 1.7% against 1.9%) and within ~1% of goodput. clamp_min guards against the counter resetting, which deriv() would otherwise render as a negative spike.
panels.title: RDMA RD

options.content:
**`operation`** is the phase: `Load` is retrieve (reads), `Store` is insert (writes). The names appear on the **LMCache** tile above.

In a `Load`-only window **NVMe WR** and **RDMA RD** read ~0 by construction - that is the read path confirming itself, not a dead query. **LMCache** and **NVMe RD** should track each other at all times, warmup included; a gap between them would mean reads served from page cache, or a brief dip at a warmup->measured transition. **RDMA WR** and **RDMA RD** come off a burst-latched ACC counter on a 5m window, so trust their trend, not a single reading.

**RDMA WR = fabric TX = payload pushed to initiators**, and it is the same bytes as **NVMe RD** one hop earlier. **RDMA RD = fabric RX = payload arriving from initiators**, same bytes as **NVMe WR**. The summary tiles and the Falcon panel below name the same two counters.

panels.title: Reading this section

panels.description: Application payload goodput reported by the running bench l2 processes on the mmg initiators. The Prometheus endpoint is short-lived and exists only while bench l2 is running. Use the end-of-run JSON and counter gate for publishable throughput; this panel aligns the workload with the target-side host and NVMe trends.
panels.title: LMCache aggregate goodput (bits/s)

panels.description: Total application payload goodput per initiator process. The Prometheus endpoint is short-lived and exists only while bench l2 is running. Operations are summed here to expose imbalance between mmgi0 and mmgi1 without combining the read and write aggregate lines.
panels.title: LMCache goodput by initiator (bits/s)

panels.description: Current completed-submit rate from the short-lived bench l2 Prometheus endpoints. No active run means the endpoints are no longer being scraped.
panels.title: LMCache completed submits/s

panels.description: Mean submit-to-completion latency over the query window from the short-lived bench l2 Prometheus endpoints. The endpoint intentionally does not expose live percentiles; use the final benchmark summary for p50/p99.

targets.expr: sum by (operation) (rate(lmcache_bench_l2_submit_latency_seconds_total{job="lmcache_bench_mmg",host=~"mmgi.*",phase="measured"}[60s]) and on (host, initiator) (up{job="lmcache_bench_mmg",host=~"mmgi.*"} == 1)) / sum by (operation) (rate(lmcache_bench_l2_completed_submits_total{job="lmcache_bench_mmg",host=~"mmgi.*",phase="measured"}[60s]) and on (host, initiator) (up{job="lmcache_bench_mmg",host=~"mmgi.*"} == 1))

panels.title: LMCache mean submit latency by operation

panels.description: PCM event classification per direction and socket, on the same >1 GB/s traffic gate as the hit % panel beside it. Log y-axis because the miss series runs two to three orders of magnitude below the hit series and is invisible on a linear scale. Not an end-to-end DDIO proof.

panels.description: Hit / (hit + miss) per direction and socket, restricted to sockets carrying more than 1 GB/s of PCIe traffic. Socket 0 holds no IPU and no exported NVMe on this box, so its denominator is a ~100 KB/s noise floor and its ratio swung 15-85% for arithmetic reasons rather than DDIO reasons; the gate removes it and would let it back in if it ever carried real traffic. On socket 1 over 01:35-01:45 UTC read held 99.5% and write 96.3%. PCM event classification, not an end-to-end DDIO proof.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (direction, socket) (pcm_pcie_bandwidth_bytes_per_second{host="mmgt",classification="hit"}) / sum by (direction, socket) (pcm_pcie_bandwidth_bytes_per_second{host="mmgt",classification=~"hit|miss"}) and on (direction, socket) (pcm_pcie_bandwidth_bytes_per_second{host="mmgt",classification="total"} > 1e9)

panels.description: PCM total PCIe bandwidth per direction and socket. Socket 1 carries everything (read 17.70 GB/s, write 16.19 GB/s mean over 01:35-01:45 UTC) and socket 0 shows 0.038 read / 0.0001 write, because both MMG-400s and all eight exported drives sit on socket 1 on this box - socket 0 has no IPU and no array member. The 500x asymmetry is the as-built topology, not a broken socket. Includes traffic this benchmark does not originate.

panels.description: The same two counters as the RDMA WR and RDMA RD tiles in the summary row, as a trend. The underlying counter latches every 30s - 34 of 40 consecutive 5s buckets were empty and the other 6 carried ~356 Gb/s each - so rate() beats against the latch period and sawtooths at any window width. This uses deriv() over 5m, a least-squares fit across every sample in the window, which reads as smooth as the payload itself (CV 1.7% against 1.9%) and within ~1% of goodput. clamp_min guards against the counter resetting, which deriv() would otherwise render as a negative spike.
